summary: Cream-colored brick keeper's house and tower in Peninsula State Park, first lit in 1868; automated in 1926 and run as a museum by the Door County Historical Society since 1963.

structures.note: Square tower, nine feet four inches on a side, built into the corner of the two-story keeper's house (LighthouseFriends; NRHP). The sources disagree on the corner.
Two-story brick keeper's house with a kitchen wing (LighthouseFriends; NRHP).
LighthouseFriends dates the brick oil house to 1890; the Board's 1899 report shows the metal still in storage.

access.note: Peninsula State Park; self-guided museum tours run by the Door County Historical Society, mid-May to mid-October, $7 per person; state park sticker required.

facts.agency: Door County Historical Society (museum operator); land in Peninsula State Park

events.note: Congress appropriates $12,000 for a light to help ships pass through Strawberry Channel (28 July 1866).
Dwelling and tower of Milwaukee brick, built 1868.
Henry Stanley first exhibits the light, 13 October 1868.
Third-and-a-half-order Fresnel by Henry-Lepaute (LighthouseFriends; the station record says third order).
William H. Duclon takes charge, 20 September 1883, after Stanley's transfer to Sherwood Point.
Brick oil house, per LighthouseFriends. The Board's 1899 report shows oil-house metal still in storage; the dates conflict.
Barn built, 16 by 24 feet, one and a half stories.
Lighthouse Service Bulletin lists the station among lights changed to incandescent oil vapor.
Third-and-a-half-order lens replaced by a fifth-order lens (LighthouseFriends).
Peter Coughlin transferred from Green Island, February 1919.
Converted to an unmanned acetylene light; Coughlin's last log entry 15 September 1926.
Fruit Growers Union Cooperative leases the dwelling as an office.
State acquires 10.98 acres for Peninsula State Park; federal government keeps the light (LighthouseFriends; the year is the start of the 1930s acquisition).
Restoration begins under the Door County Historical Society with Coast Guard permission (LighthouseFriends; NRHP 1961-1963).
Door County Historical Society opens the lighthouse as a museum.
NRHP nomination prepared; it names the Coast Guard and the state as owners.
Lighthouse transferred to the State of Wisconsin (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the original lens was a third-and-a-half-order Fresnel, replaced in 1918 by a fifth-order lens. The USLHS place record (Original Optic Type: THIRD & ONE HALF ORDER) confirms it. The record's 'order 3' is therefore wrong for the original lens. Proposed for editor review; not applied.

notes_for_editor: CHECKED 2026-10-22. Quotes: 68 found on the first run. UNRESOLVED: (1) Oil house: LighthouseFriends says a Lighthouse Board crew built a brick oil house in 1890; the Board's 1899 report says the metal work for the oil house was bought and stored at Sturgeon Bay Canal for delivery 'as soon as practicable'. The story states that the two do not agree. (2) Tower corner: LighthouseFriends northwest; NRHP 'at the northeast' (checked; both stated). (3) Original lens: LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record both say third-and-a-half order (checked); the record's 'order 3' is an error for the original lens (see corrections). (4) Owner and transfer: NRHP (1970) names 'Federal/State (U.S. Coast Guard; Wis. Dept. of Natural Resources)'; LighthouseFriends says the state received the lighthouse in 2003. (5) Restoration start: LighthouseFriends 1961; NRHP 1961-1963 (checked). (6) Stanley's 1881 log entry is quoted by LighthouseFriends; the log itself was not read. (7) No storms, wrecks or rescues are sourced for this station in the sources read, so the 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter is omitted. (8) The NRHP cites a Milwaukee Sentinel article (1963) and a Green Bay Press-Gazette article (1965) and Frances Badtke's 1944 book; none was read. No newspaper search was run. (9) Tour hours: the Door County Historical Society page (11 a.m. to 4 p.m., mid-May to mid-October, $7 per person, state park sticker required) is used; LighthouseFriends' older 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. is not. (10) Privacy: Duclon family members, the Stanley family's doctor, and 2003-era staff are not named. The DCHS and the Coast Guard are named as organisations. (11) Wikipedia consulted as a lead only; not cited. (12) Fiscal-year fixes applied: the 1893 and 1899 Board reports are labelled as fiscal years.
